blocks.text: How did we build a story from fragmented archival records?

Story-building examines how historical fragments are transformed into narratives. We set ourselves one rule from the start: the documents in the archive were the only material. Nothing would be invented to fill the gaps.
"Archival material is documented reality. Distilling a narrative from it required committing to the actual past. We were not writing a story but engraving it." — Amit
"This was not a fictional story. Our research mission was to sonify the archive, that is, to mediate what had already been written and documented through sound." — Tzlil
